primary_sources.title: Liste der österreichischen Doppelbesteuerungsabkommen
primary_sources.use: authoritative treaty-universe inventory and links to current treaty/protocol/synthesized texts

primary_sources.title: Multilaterales Instrument
primary_sources.use: Austria MLI instrument, reservations and notifications
primary_sources.caution: Pair-specific matching and withholding-tax effective dates must be established relationship by relationship; Austria-side notification alone is not sufficient to infer bilateral effect.

primary_sources.title: Einkommensteuergesetz 1988 § 93
primary_sources.use: capital-yield withholding-tax obligation and corporate-recipient KESt rate framework
primary_sources.relevant_observation: Section 93 imposes KESt on domestic capital income; for corporate KESt debtors the withholding agent may apply 23% to income received from 2024 onward.

primary_sources.title: Einkommensteuergesetz 1988 § 94
primary_sources.use: exceptions from KESt withholding, including EU parent-company dividend relief
primary_sources.relevant_observation: Foreign EU qualifying parent companies may obtain no-withholding treatment for qualifying dividends where the statutory conditions are met, including at least 10% participation and an uninterrupted one-year holding period; anti-abuse/refund safeguards remain relevant.

primary_sources.title: Einkommensteuergesetz 1988 § 99
primary_sources.use: special withholding tax for limited taxpayers; seed source for royalty/right-use analysis
primary_sources.caution: The exact mapping of standard TaxTreat royalty categories to the current § 99 enumerated items must be completed before runtime promotion.

primary_sources.title: Einkommensteuergesetz 1988 § 100
primary_sources.use: rate and withholding mechanics for § 99 withholding tax
primary_sources.relevant_observation: The standard § 99 withholding-tax rate is 20%, subject to the special categories listed in § 100.

primary_sources.title: Entlastung von österreichischen Abzugsteuern an der Quelle
primary_sources.use: procedural framework for treaty relief at source under the DBA-Entlastungsverordnung
primary_sources.caution: Relief at source is documentation- and case-dependent and is excluded for specified recipient/situation categories; these procedural constraints must not be collapsed into treaty-rate eligibility.

interest.candidate_regime: domestic-source and KESt scope require instrument/category-specific analysis under §§ 27, 93-95 and limited-taxpayer source rules

royalty.candidate_regime: special withholding under §§ 99-100 EStG 1988 where the statutory category applies

release_constraints: No Austrian treaty rate, domestic rate, exemption, deadline or filing obligation is released by this inventory.
AT must remain unregistered in the production source-country registry until domestic, treaty, MLI, calculation, compliance and release evidence are complete.
Every treaty instrument and protocol must be resolved to official primary text before promotion.
MLI matching and WHT-effective dates must be determined treaty by treaty.
The interest scope must remain fail-closed until Austrian domestic-source and withholding applicability are mapped by instrument/category.
Treaty relief eligibility and the procedural ability to grant relief at source under the DBA-Entlastungsverordnung are distinct layers and must be modelled separately.
